newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CANBERRA WATCH-Budget bills update for Dec 3 - overview.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CANBERRA WATCH-Budget bills update for Dec 3 - overview.

text.p: Another day passes without the Senate finishing a significant budget bill, and budget watchers still wonder how much of the A$7.2 billion budget cuts will survive.

The total at risk is the rather impressive sum of A$2 billion. That is, the government will very probably need unpredictable Independent support for budget measures that are worth A$2 billion to the 1997/98 budget.

At the moment the Senate is still considering the bill to raise students' university charges and the rate at which they pay off their debts. That bill alone is worth about A$300 million to the 1997/98 budget.
It was supposed to be finished last week, then Monday, then today and now tomorrow.
According to current planning the following bill will be a relatively uncontroversial package of tax legislation and then Telstra, which the government says it wants finished this week.
It might take the rest of the week.
If that happens, the Senate will slide towards its Friday 13th end-of-sittings deadline still with almost A$2 billion of fiscal tightening in the balance.

Canberra Watch has discovered (a little late, and we apologise) that a contentious moderate-sized budget measure can now be counted as a definite survivor of the Senate: a set of regulations to tighten eligibility for the childcare tax rebate.
This measure is worth A$43 million in 1997/98.
Labor and Democrat senators tried to overrule the ministerial regulations that gave effect to the measure, but the government held them off with Independent support.
